articles.title: Has Pakistan reopened its border with Iran for trade?
articles.summary: Traders say some exports are crossing border after a weeklong halt, but Tehran says its cargo is not getting through.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan – On a normal day, hundreds of freight trucks and vehicles pass through Pakistan-Iran border crossings, carrying goods and people. On October 17, Islamabad suspended cargo traffic through the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings in Balochistan province, citing security risks.

On Monday, some goods started to move again.

Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, president of the Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry, told Al Jazeera that trade “partially resumed this weekend”.

Border officials also cleared consignments that were dated from October 16 or earlier, goods truck association officials said.

Haji Noor Muhammad Shahwani, central president of the Balochistan Goods Truck Owners Association, told Al Jazeera from Quetta that Pakistani exports such as rice and bananas were crossing the border.

Trucks loaded in Iran before the closure, including those carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), were also entering Pakistan, he confirmed to Al Jazeera. “Those that were already loaded are clearing and coming out now. They are coming slowly.”

The halt of Iranian LPG to Pakistan created severe shortages and price spikes in Pakistan, which imports the bulk of its energy from the Middle East. Pakistan’s economy has already been impacted by shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz caused by Iran and its response to the United States-Israel war.

Rizwan Ahmed, a customs clearing agent based near the Gabd-Rimdan crossing said customs had told agents to file declarations for the stranded trucks, which would then be released.

“Customs has given us the go-ahead, saying, ‘Bring in as much cargo as you can,’” Ahmed told Al Jazeera. He did not say whether this applied to goods loaded after October 16.

Ahmed said his own consignment of exports had just left. “We have rice, retail goods, potatoes, bananas,” he told Al Jazeera.

But Iran said changes to import paperwork introduced by Islamabad are holding up its cargo at the crossings.

On Sunday, Iran’s ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, said on X that Iran had placed no restrictions on exports to Pakistan, including LPG, and its borders remained open.

“Changes in the implementation of Pakistan’s E-Form procedure for imports from Iran have created a situation in which traders are effectively and literally unable to dispatch cargo from Iran to Pakistan,” he wrote.

The halt in trade between the two neighbours triggered speculation that the Pakistani step might have been taken under US pressure as part of Washington’s efforts to suffocate Iran economically. Pakistan insisted it was done amid a deteriorating security situation in Balochistan province on the border with Iran.

Gunmen attacked trucks waiting near the Gabd crossing on the Pakistani side of the border on Thursday. The military said 10 attackers were killed in operations around Gabd and Gwadar city, and one civilian died.

The attack came in a province that has faced a separatist rebellion for decades.

Balochistan accounted for 131 of the 225 armed attacks recorded nationwide in September, the highest monthly national total in 12 years, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs was asked about the border at its weekly news briefing on Friday.

“Pakistan, as a responsible member of the international community, adheres to and shall continue to adhere to all applicable sanctions regimes in accordance with international and domestic laws,” spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan said.

He said he did not have direct knowledge of the situation on the ground. He did not say whether the border was open or whether the US had pressured Pakistan over the closure.

The Ministry of Commerce did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

A Commerce Ministry memorandum from October 16, seen by Al Jazeera, withdrew its October 3 memorandum extending a waiver on the E-Form, also called the EIF, for imports from Iran. It took effect immediately.

The purpose of the E-Form is to record imports and their payment through banks.

Moghadam, the Iranian envoy, said consultations with Pakistan were under way. Citing reports, he added that several hundred LPG trucks had crossed into Gabd but were yet to be unloaded or cleared.

Shahwani, from the Balochistan Goods Truck Owners Association, said the unloading problem had not been resolved.

“It is probably some problem with the banks, something to do with international trade,” he said.

Bakhtiar Ismail, the deputy commissioner of Chagai in Balochistan, wrote on X on October 18 that the closure was a temporary measure to improve border management and support counterterrorism efforts.

Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei cited technical issues, according to the IRNA news agency.

Pakistan has mediated between Washington and Tehran since the US-Israel war on Iran began on February 28. The US has since imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, impacting Iranian exports. The US has also imposed wide-ranging economic sanctions to “asphyxiate” the Iranian government and cut off its revenue streams.

Imtiaz Baloch, a security analyst who focuses on Balochistan, told Al Jazeera that the US policy of maximum pressure on Iran had a direct or indirect influence.

That could be done directly, by forcing Pakistan’s government to close the border, or indirectly, through companies in the LPG trade or international banking channels, he said. But he added that no concrete or visible statement had linked the closure to US economic policy.

“My assessment is that security is part of it, procedures or technical glitches are part of it and the banking system is also involved,” Baloch said.

articles.title: A Trump-appointed appeals judge questioned a DOJ bid to set aside California mail ballots linked to 20,000 suspected noncitizens; no decision has been issued yet
articles.summary: A Trump-appointed appeals court judge on Sunday questioned the Justice Department’s bid to force California to set aside mail-in ballots linked to around
articles.body: A Trump-appointed appeals court judge on Sunday questioned the Justice Department’s bid to force California to set aside mail-in ballots linked to around 20,000 suspected noncitizens, raising doubts over the Trump administration’s legal challenge ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.During a rare weekend hearing, two of the three judges on the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals appeared sceptical of the administration’s arguments, questioning the legal basis for its demand and whether the appeals court could intervene before a lower court ruling. The panel said it would try to deliver a decision as quickly as possible.The Justice Department wants California officials to separate ballots associated with people identified by the administration as likely noncitizens and prevent them from being counted until their citizenship status is verified.Trump administration’s push faces constitutional questionsJudge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, questioned whether the administration’s demand conflicted with the US Constitution’s Elections Clause, which gives states the authority to determine the time, place and manner of congressional elections.“It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law that the California legislature has adopted pursuant to the Elections Clause,” Bennett told Justice Department lawyer Matthew Donnelly, according to Reuters.The administration argued that California was causing irreparable harm by allowing suspected noncitizens to vote in violation of state law. Donnelly also contended that the lower court’s schedule was too slow, given that election officials were processing thousands of mail ballots daily.Judge Gabriel Sanchez, appointed by former President Joe Biden, questioned whether the appeals court had the authority to intervene before the lower court had ruled on the matter. A hearing in the district court has been scheduled for October 27.Judge Patrick Bumatay, another Trump appointee, said ensuring that only eligible citizens vote was in everyone’s interest and suggested that an emergency order could provide clarity.California challenges reliability of voter listThe lawsuit, filed by the Justice Department on October 15, alleges that California officials failed to comply with a 48-hour deadline to review the names flagged by the federal government.California has disputed the administration’s claims, arguing that its safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and that the federal list contains unreliable information.An attorney representing Los Angeles County Clerk Dean Logan said a review of 200 records from the administration’s list found cancelled or inactive registrations, people with no voting history and individuals who appeared to have been born in the US.The county also warned that checking ballots against the list could impose a significant administrative burden and risk disenfranchising eligible voters.Midterm battle over election oversightThe dispute comes as Republicans narrowly control both chambers of Congress and Democrats seek to regain the House in the November midterms. California, a Democratic stronghold, holds 52 seats in the House of Representatives.The Trump administration has stepped up efforts to obtain voter-registration information from states, arguing that stricter checks are necessary to protect election integrity. Critics have accused it of overstepping federal authority.Noncitizen voting remains exceedingly rare. A Reuters investigation published in July found 129 cases in which noncitizens had been federally charged with illegal voting, with many cases appearing to involve confusion or administrative errors rather than intentional fraud.You use AI every day. articles.title: The State that Elon Musk tells every company in America to move to has suspended 17 data center construction permits over …
articles.summary: Texas, the business-friendly destination that tech billionaire Elon Musk routinely urges American companies to relocate to, has suspended the construction
articles.body: Texas, the business-friendly destination that tech billionaire Elon Musk routinely urges American companies to relocate to, has suspended the construction permits for 17 data center projects and taken an automated approval portal offline after state regulators discovered permits were still being handed out weeks after an official freeze was ordered. The intervention comes after Texas governor Greg Abbott called for a complete halt on new data center approvals in September 2026. Despite that directive, automated systems continued approving applications, prompting public reports from watchdog groups FracTracker Alliance and Public Citizen that revealed more than two dozen approvals had slipped through the cracks, according to a report by 404 Media.In response, state regulators pulled the plug on the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality’s (TCEQ) automated licensing software, known as STEERS (State of Texas Environmental Electronic Reporting System). A notice posted on the state website confirmed the shutdown:“TCEQ’s electronic filing application used for automatic authorizations has been temporarily shut down to ensure all applications are reviewed by agency staff to determine if they are related to data centers.”Automated portal kept ‘rubber-stamping’ mega-projectsThe STEERS platform had long functioned as a digital mechanism to quickly grant routine construction clearances. However, when Abbott instructed agencies to pause new data center authorisations, state officials failed to take the automated software offline. As a result, applications continued moving forward without manual administrative oversight.All 17 of the suspended authorisations involve stormwater construction permits, which is a mandatory regulatory step in Texas where builders level and grade the earth. Securing this clearance is an essential requirement for nearly any major commercial construction development to proceed legally in the state.Abbott audits 1,800 facilities to protect grid and water resourcesThe permit freeze follows Governor Abbott’s decision to put the brakes on roughly 1,800 data center projects across Texas while state agencies conduct exhaustive operational audits. The widespread pause was prompted by mounting alarms over the massive energy and water demands of high-density computing hubs, as well as their broader environmental consequences for neighboring towns.“Our top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life. Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT, and by state law, must be denied connection to the Texas grid. Simply put, Texans must come first,” Governor Abbott said in an earlier statement explaining the audit.Under the governor’s directives, any proposed facility failing to meet the standards set by the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT), the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), and state statutes will be formally blocked from linking up to the Texas electrical grid.Earlier this year, a report claimed that Texas is all set to become the world’s new data center capital. Research from Jones Lang LaSalle (JLL) claimed that the state is on track to surpass Virginia as the world’s largest data market by 2030. articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO countdown: Who are the tech giants funding the AI powerhouse, and how much?
articles.summary: With Anthropic announcing its US IPO, attention is turning to the tech giants that have poured billions of dollars into the AI company behind Claude.
articles.body: With Anthropic announcing its US IPO, attention is turning to the tech giants that have poured billions of dollars into the AI company behind Claude.The startup has filed to list its shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the offering.According to Reuters, Amazon and Google are among Anthropic’s major financial backers, investing billions of dollars in the startup while also providing the cloud computing infrastructure needed to develop and run its AI models.The company’s IPO filing highlights how closely Anthropic’s growth is tied to these technology giants, which are also competitors in the AI market.Amazon has invested $8 billion in Anthropic previously and announced another $5 billion investment, with the option to invest up to an additional $20 billion in the future, according to Anthropic's April 2026 announcement.If the full additional amount is invested, Amazon's total investment would reach $33 billion. Reuters reported that Anthropic plans to spend at least $111.1 billion with Google on infrastructure over the next seven to 10 years.Anthropic has also partnered with Google and chip designer Broadcom to expand access to Google's tensor processing units (TPUs), which are used to train and run AI models.Nvidia's involvement includes both a potential IPO investment and an earlier strategic partnership. articles.summary: Four people died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford, was set on fire earlier this month.
articles.body:
A man in his 20s, who was arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, has been released without charge.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford, was set on fire earlier this month.

A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

On Saturday, gardaí (Irish police) said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday were released without charge .

Gardaí said investigations into the attack are ongoing.

articles.title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan
articles.summary: Prosecutors have indicted Devin Jacob Ballard for a killing that has caused outrage in Japan, local media reports.
articles.body:
A US Marine has been indicted on suspicion of murdering and robbing a woman in Japan earlier this month in a case that has triggered protests, Japanese media reports.

Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was arrested on suspicion of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa.

Prosecutors have now indicted him for allegedly strangling Yagi with a telephone cord and then stealing her backpack and wallet on 3 October, media reports, citing the indictment document.

It wasreported Ballard had denied the allegations, but Asahi Shimbun and Kyodo News cited investigators saying he has made some statements suggesting involvement.

Security footage allegedly shows a man believed to be the suspect entering the hotel with the woman and leaving alone with her belongings.

Yagi's death has caused outrage in Japan, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi describing the crime as "brutal and heinous".

Earlier this month, the Marine Corps said it was "actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine" and extended condolences to the victim's family.

It is the latest case involving a US serviceman in Okinawa, which hosts the highest concentration of around 55,000 US soldiers stationed in Japan.

Previous criminal cases have sparked anger and protests, the largest of which took place in 1995, when tens of thousands took to the streets following the abduction, beating and rape of a 12-year-old girl.

In 2024 alone, there were four sexual assault cases involving US troops in Okinawa, including that of air force member Brennon Washington, who was given five years for the rape and kidnapping of an underage girl.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja said the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

The prime minister said her government has registered a "strong" protest with the US and called for "strict disciplinary action against US military personnel and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents".

People in Japan have been voicing anger, with some 100 people protesting in both Naha and Tokyo earlier this month. Others took to social media expressing their outrage and demanding justice, with one user saying: "Enough is enough."

articles.title: Oxford Street fills with shoppers on first traffic-free day
articles.summary: Almost 1km of the popular shopping destination is pedestrianised between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street.
articles.body:
Part of Oxford Street has been pedestrianised, with visitors experiencing the first day that cars, taxis, buses and bicycles have been banned from some of the central London street .

Almost 1km (0.62-mile) of the popular shopping destination has been pedestrianised between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street by the mayor's Oxford Street Development Corporation .

The change has been welcomed by some shoppers, although questions have been raised about how accessible it will be for disabled visitors.

London's mayor Lord Sadiq Khan said it was a "momentous day for London", and the changes were the first phase in lifting the street out of "decline".

The roll-out was met with some confusion as many cyclists continued to pedal through the newly-installed barriers, with some being shouted at by security staff to "dismount" and walk their route instead.

Whether this is a teething problem or a constant enforcement issue remains to be seen in the weeks and months to come.

A police officer was also seen getting to grips with the new arrangement, as he asked an Oxford Street security worker: "How do I get my car down there?"

But as shoppers started to descend on the street, many celebrated the change.

Lucia, who works nearby, said she took a detour to see the newly pedestrianised street.

"It's very joyful," she said. "We are used to walking on crowded pavements, so it's really exciting to see the people using this space."

"Let's see how it regenerates with time, how different types of businesses pop out, how different spaces for people to hang out appear.

"I think in summer it will be lovely. Christmas will be great, it will be more enjoyable."

Her views were echoed by others, and as the day went on, more people could be seen walking on the newly changed road rather than sticking to the pavement.

However, concerns were raised by some about accessibility, and whether the re-routed buses and new bus stops and taxi ranks, installed about 200m and 100m from the pedestrianised area respectively, would be enough to support disabled shoppers.

One black cab driver who spoke to BBC London said he was worried that access to Oxford Street would "become a problem" for some of his disabled passengers.

Last week, chair of Inclusion London, Adam Gabsi, said "the proof will be in the pudding".

"If access to buses and taxis becomes difficult, then there'll be problems for people like me," he said, adding that although disabled Londoners were consulted on the plan, it was not co-produced by them.

Sight loss charity Guide Dogs welcomed the changes, and Wheels for Wellbeing argued that accessibility needed to be properly built into the final design.

Michael Bolt, from the Marylebone Association, was among a number of locals who said they feared surrounding areas would be "ruined" as traffic was displaced on to other roads.

Karen Jones, who has lived in the area for 20 years, also said she was worried what would happen to their "beautiful garden neighbourhoods".

Lord Khan said he wanted people to be "in charge" of Oxford Street, not traffic, and hoped it would become a site for "culture, leisure and tourism".

"This is a street that has been known as the nation's high street for more than 100 years," he said.

"Over the last couple of decades it's been in decline.

"I'm not willing to stand by as shops leave this street, as jobs leave this street, and that's why I'm really proud 1km of this street is traffic free."

The mayor said the area would be "safe and spacious" in the lead-up to Christmas, with more improvement works coming in the new year.

"We're going to carry on testing and learning, refining the plans we have to make sure everyone gets to enjoy this street," he said.

"We don't want it to be horrible, we want it to be great.

"We are going to learn from this first phase to make sure the next phase takes on people's concerns."

Seb Dance, London's deputy mayor for transport and deputy chair for Transport for London (TfL), said "people will see very quickly the benefits" of pedestrianisation.

TfL previously told BBC London it expected to see "a manageable increase in traffic" on Wigmore Street, Cavendish Place, Henrietta Street, Marylebone Lane and Welbeck Street.

Tim Barnes, deputy leader of Westminster City Council, said residents had regularly raised issues with pedestrianisation of Oxford Street whenever a scheme was proposed in the past.

"We just couldn't find ways that would practically work," he said.

"I think we need to see a lot of how this works in practice. We will be monitoring for traffic problems or noise problems, pollution issues, and taking those back to TfL and the mayor, and charging them with the responsibility of fixing those problems if they've created them."

The Oxford Street Development Corporation, which is leading the change, previously said it had worked with the emergency services to understand their access needs to Oxford Street, and would continue to do so as the changes unfold.

It said police, ambulances and the fire service would be able to access the pedestrianised areas along "multiple access points".

What is walking down the newly pedestrianised Oxford Street like?

The project, which is estimated to cost about £150m, will see gradual changes unfold along the road, with road surfaces being raised, trees and seating installed, and traffic lights rephased.

The corporation said "possible future phases are being considered and costed".

Kate Boothman Meier, director of corporate affairs at New West End Company, said: "The ultimate aim is to try and pedestrianise the wider Oxford Street. That is further down the line, we have to see how this goes first."

Additional reporting by James W Kelly, Gem O'Reilly, Lauren Stanley from BBC London and Tom Edwards, BBC London transport correspondent.

articles.title: RNLI statue will not be installed at Porthmeor beach in Cornwall
articles.summary: The lifesaver sculpture will not be unveiled at Porthmeor after opposition from the town council.
articles.body:
A bronze statue of an RNLI lifeguard will no longer be installed at a popular beach after a town council opposed plans for the artwork.

Cornwall Council originally approved the charity's planning application for the artwork on the rocky foreshore at Porthmeor beach in St Ives.

But the plans were opposed by St Ives Town Council, which said the figurative portrayal of the lifesaver was "related to another Cornish town" and the "selection of St Ives... appears to have been arbitrary".

The RNLI said the sculpture would no longer be situated at Porthmeor and "several coastal locations" were being considered as alternatives, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

The bronze sculpture by Zennor-based artist Holly Bendall, entitled Let Not The Deep Swallow Me Up, shows a female RNLI lifeguard standing watch over the sea.

It was inspired by the actions of RNLI lifeguard Sophie Grant-Crookston , who, in 2006, became the first female lifeguard to receive a Medal of Gallantry in recognition of her bravery after saving a surfer's life in Perranporth.

Councillor Andrew Mitchell, who represents St Ives on Cornwall Council, said although he had the "greatest respect" for the RNLI he believed the scupture was "definitely the wrong thing in the wrong place".

"I can confirm that although Cornwall Council granted planning permission on an officer decision, the RNLI is no longer going to proceed at Porthmeor," he said.

He said the RNLI had negotiated with Perranzabuloe Parish Council to have the statue placed there as the lifesaver's home town but the parish council and the RNLI could not confirm it would be unveiled on Perranporth beach or another nearby location.

Councillor Paul Viney, chairman of St Ives Town Council's planning committee, said members felt the scale and design of the sculpture "did not enhance the proposed setting on Porthmeor beach" and the story was "not related" to St Ives.

He said the committee understood the sculpture "will not be sited in St Ives but in the village of Perranporth, the home of the lifesaver depicted in the design".

Bendall said last month she and the RNLI were "disheartened" by the town council's opposition, but were looking forward to seeing the sculpture become "a lasting tribute to the RNLI and the community it serves".

The RNLI said: "Several coastal locations are being considered as possible sites for the sculpture.

"A variety of factors are being taken into account. A final decision is yet to be made."

articles.title: NYPD detective stabbed 10 times in Bronx robbery recalls chasing attackers while bleeding out
articles.summary: Detective Jose Mercedes reveals on "One Nation" how his blood-soaked phone prevented him from calling 911 while chasing attackers in the Bronx.
articles.body: An NYPD detective stabbed 10 times during a robbery in the Bronx revealed how he struggled to call 911 while tracking his fleeing attackers before recognizing the severity of his own injuries and the extent of his blood loss Sunday on "One Nation with Brian Kilmeade." Detective Jose Mercedes said in an exclusive interview with Fox News that he couldn't unlock his phone as he tried to report his attackers' whereabouts. Realizing that he was bleeding badly, he stopped following them — recalling cases he had investigated involving victims who suffered significant blood loss."Suddenly, I grabbed my phone again, and it's completely filled with blood," Mercedes said. "And at that point is when I stopped running." Mercedes said his police training kicked in when two masked men approached him while he was retrieving belongings from his car's trunk on his day off work. One displayed a knife and attempted to grab the gold chains around his neck. ‘BONNIE AND CLYDE’ ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT COUPLE ACCUSED OF BRAZEN JEWELRY THEFT SPREE ACROSS FOUR STATES "The first thing that went through my mind was fear," Mercedes recalled. "The next thing that went through my mind was action." Mercedes said he managed to unmask both suspects during the struggle, despite fearing they might have additional weapons. He also said he would have tried to escape the confrontation if he had seen the men approaching. "The fear that comes upon you and your body turns cold," he told host Brian Kilmeade. "Thereafter, your adrenaline kicks in. And now it’s action time, and now I have to defend myself with all my might or die." ILLEGAL SUSPECT IN NYPD DETECTIVE STABBING DENIES INVOLVEMENT AFTER EXTRADITION FROM MASSACHUSETTS Police identified the alleged attackers as D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24. articles.title: Mecca defence alliance members in Tehran to defuse Iran-US, Yemen tensions
articles.summary: Countering Houthi advances in Yemen will be a major focus for Saudi Arabia and its allies in Tehran.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Ministers and senior security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – the three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement – are in Tehran to discuss regional security issues amid threats of new US strikes on Iran.

Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani military chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and will discuss tensions with security chief Mohsen Rezaei.

The meetings are among the highest-profile dialogues held in Tehran in recent months. While there is still little information on what might be discussed, the meetings come amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to deal with a new escalation between the United States and Iran .

But analysts broadly believe the visit to Tehran by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a regional defence alliance, will be enough to prevent a new outbreak in violence between the US and Iran.

“The Mecca pact’s 11th-hour visit to Tehran is an attempt to tip the balance in favour of those willing to compromise before the guns start blazing again,” said Ali Vaez, deputy director of the Middle East and North Africa Program at the International Crisis Group.

“But unless they arrive with a credible formula to bridge the US-Iran divide, they may find themselves with little more than goodwill in a race against the clock.”

The talks are expected to address the waves of missile and drone attacks carried out by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, who are allied with Tehran, on Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

“I believe that parties to the Mecca agreement lack options of military engagement with the Houthis, but Riyadh is certainly asserting greater pressure for more, and its expectation of its partners has grown in parallel with the offensive from Yemen,” Ayesha Siddiqa, a senior research fellow in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera.

But despite the collective security arrangement in the Mecca defence pact, Saudi Arabia’s allies Turkiye and Pakistan cannot “afford to commit troops on the ground” in Yemen, said Siddiqa.

The latest diplomatic push is likely linked to visits by Pakistani army chief Asim Munir to Saudi Arabia and Iran last week, Siddiqa said, and coincides with Islamabad’s restrictions on overland border trade with Tehran amid the US blockade on Iran.

Iranian authorities have said they favoured “security originating from within the region” as they prepared for the meetings.

Umer Karim, who researches Saudi foreign policy and its implications for regional security, said the Tehran meetings are unlikely to reduce the risk of a renewed war between Iran and the US, which would likely lead to more regional turmoil.

“Therefore, these talks perhaps are more concerned about the security of Saudi Arabia and involve an attempt by Turkiye and Pakistan to compel Iran to reach a compromise,” he told Al Jazeera.

US President Donald Trump is said to be considering new attacks to break the diplomatic deadlock with Iran, which has refused to agree to any peace agreement with Washington unless several of its demands are met.

The US and regional powers want international shipping and transit through the Strait of Hormuz to resume without impediments or attacks. Washington also wants to rein in Tehran’s nuclear programme and bring in international inspectors to assess Iran’s highly enriched uranium . Israel says it wants to overthrow the Islamic Republic.

Tehran wants to lift the US naval blockade of Iran’s southern ports, which has halted crude oil exports and disrupted most trade, and return to a memorandum of understanding agreed between the two countries in June.

The US has refused this, with President Trump saying he is left with a choice to “finish the job” by launching major strikes on Iran’s civilian infrastructure. This could prompt Iran to lash out at its neighbours, as it did earlier in the war with strikes on US bases in Arab states and infrastructure.

Meanwhile, the US Department of State issued an October 21 order for nonemergency US government employees and their family ⁠members to leave Saudi Arabia for their safety’s sake, given the Houthi threat.

As talks involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye continue in Iran, analysts say these Mecca Joint Defence Agreement signatories will likely try to minimise the impact on Saudi Arabia if war does break out again.

“However, since little has changed from an Iranian strategic calculus and the actors involved don’t have the kind of leverage needed to affect Iran’s strategic thinking, these negotiations are going to yield little,” Karim said.

articles.title: Ponguleti unveils plan for developing Nelakondapalli stupa as Buddhist tourism hub
articles.summary: Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy announces plan to develop Nelakondapalli 3rd-century Buddhist stupa into an international tourism hub, with restoration and facilities.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Revenue and housing minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy on Monday announced plans to develop the 3rd-century Buddhist stupa at Nelakondapalli in Palair constituency into an international Buddhist tourism hub, with a focus on restoring the historic monument and creating tourism infrastructure.The minister laid the foundation for various development works aimed at preserving the Buddhist site and improving facilities in the surrounding areas. He said the stupa, discovered around 50 years ago, is one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the country.He said previous govts had initiated development works in the area but failed to complete them. Archaeological excavations within a 1.5-km radius of the stupa had unearthed several ancient artefacts. However, owing to the lack of local facilities for their preservation, the artefacts were shifted to a museum in Hyderabad.On the directions of chief minister A Revanth Reddy, a meeting would be organised with Buddhist representatives from across the world, local community members, experts in Buddhist monuments and concerned officials to discuss the future development of the historic site, he said.During his visit to the Palair constituency, the minister also announced that all pending bills under the Indiramma housing scheme across Telangana would be credited directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts within 10 days.At Rythu Vedika in Nelakondapalli, Srinivasa Reddy distributed sanction letters to beneficiaries under the second phase of the Indiramma housing scheme in the mandal. Referring to the rainfall deficit caused by the El Niño effect, the minister expressed concern over the challenges facing farmers due to possible shortages of electricity and water. He advised farmers against taking up a second crop to avoid potential financial losses.Earlier, the minister laid the foundation for a 2.5-km bituminous road connecting Anasagaram and Pammi in Nelakondapalli mandal at an estimated cost of Rs. 2.80 crore. He subsequently inaugurated a newly constructed gram panchayat office building at Gorillapadu Thanda in Kusumanchi mandal.He also urged Congress workers to intensify voter registration to ensure party candidate Ramreddy Sarvotham Reddy’s victory with a majority of first-preference votes in the Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda graduate MLC election.Addressing a preparatory meeting in the Palair constituency, he called for registering eligible graduates. He urged party workers to counter BRS and BJP propaganda blaming Congress for drought conditions caused by El Niño. articles.title: Former Israeli PM emerges as wild card in high-stakes election with Middle East's future at stake
articles.summary: Naftali Bennett's Middle East vision includes expanding the Abraham Accords, but polls show him trailing Gadi Eisenkot and Prime Minister Netanyahu ahead of Israel's election.
articles.body: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett is seeking a political comeback with an ambitious vision for the Middle East: expanding the Abraham Accords, building economic partnerships with Arab nations and rebuilding Israel's strained international relationships, particularly with the United States. For Bennett, whose American parents moved to Israel from San Francisco, the U.S. connection is both personal and political. The 54-year-old former technology entrepreneur, a familiar face on American television, believes his business background could help him work with President Donald Trump to advance regional diplomacy. "He was a businessman, not a career politician, same as me," Bennett told The Times of Israel in June, referring to Trump. "His worldview is, let's get stuff done. Let's look at results, not process. And that's precisely my view." TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS Bennett said he would aggressively pursue regional agreements through economic cooperation, seeking to build on the U.S.-brokered Abraham Accords. But while his ambitions overlap with Trump's regional agenda, the president endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election on Oct. 18. Bennett also faces an unusual political challenge at home. His joint Beyachad, or Together, party with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid is polling behind both Netanyahu's Likud and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party. A Channel 12 poll published Oct. 23 projected 23 Knesset seats for Eisenkot, 21 for Netanyahu and 15 for Bennett and Lapid. Yet Bennett knows better than most Israeli politicians that leading the largest party is not necessary to become prime minister. In 2021, he took office despite his Yamina party winning just seven of the Knesset's 120 seats, demonstrating the power of coalition negotiations in Israel's parliamentary system. FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER How a seven-seat leader became prime minister Born in Haifa to American immigrants, Bennett served in Israel's elite Sayeret Matkal and Maglan military units before co-founding cybersecurity company Cyota, which was sold for $145 million in 2005. He entered politics as Netanyahu's chief of staff, later led the Yesha Council representing West Bank settlements and served as economy, education and defense minister. A religious Zionist and longtime opponent of Palestinian statehood, Bennett stunned Israel's political establishment in 2021 when he formed a coalition spanning right-wing, centrist, left-wing and Arab parties, ending Netanyahu's 12 consecutive years in power. The coalition collapsed in 2022, leaving many former supporters accusing him of betraying his electoral promises. WHO IS ITAMAR BEN-GVIR, THE ISRAELI FIREBRAND RISING WITH THE POPULIST RIGHT ACROSS THE GLOBE? Einat Halevy Levin, a strategic advisor who has known Bennett for years, described a politician who has spent his time outside office preparing for a second opportunity. "In 2021, he wasn't prepared. He hadn't built a governing party; he had built another election campaign," Halevy Levin told Fox News Digital. She said she met Bennett at his home in November 2023, following the Oct. 7 Hamas attack, when he had decided to return to politics. This time, according to Halevy Levin, Bennett spent years building a political organization, carefully screening candidates and developing the infrastructure needed to govern. "I've known him since he was economy minister. He was always daring and full of creative ideas, but was more inclined to stick to his own views," she said. "He has undergone a transformation." IS ISRAEL REALLY ISOLATED? POLLS AND DIPLOMACY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS A new Middle East vision meets old divisions Bennett's regional ambitions reflect an approach to diplomacy shaped by his business experience, according to Halevy Levin. She recalled attending a meeting with a senior official from a neighboring country who appeared astonished by Bennett's detailed knowledge of its economy and priorities. "He wasn't looking at the country through a military lens," she said, describing Bennett's focus on identifying shared economic interests rather than approaching every regional relationship primarily as a security challenge. In an interview with Israel's Channel 13 on Sunday, two days before the election, Bennett pointed to his meetings as prime minister with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Jordan's King Abdullah II and UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed as examples of the diplomacy he hopes to revive. He argued that Israel needs to present a new vision of a Middle Eastern renaissance and identified extremist settler violence in the West Bank as a major source of damage to its international standing. "We need to eliminate Jewish terrorism in Judea and Samaria, and I say this precisely as a supporter of the settlement movement," Bennett said. "They do not represent the overwhelming majority of settlers, but right now this is the problem causing us the greatest damage internationally." Bennett said he would direct Israel's senior police, military and intelligence officials to produce a plan within three days to crack down on extremist violence. His foreign policy, however, remains firmly on the Israeli right. On Iran, Bennett has promoted his "Octopus Doctrine," advocating direct action against Tehran rather than focusing exclusively on Iranian-backed groups. "If Hezbollah fires at us, we strike Iran," he declared at an Aug. 19 policy conference. On Gaza, Bennett opposes Palestinian statehood and supports maintaining Israeli security control until Hamas is disarmed. He has also proposed excluding Qatar and Turkey from Gaza's future arrangements while involving Egypt. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Those positions raise questions about how significantly his government would depart from Netanyahu's policies. Danny Citrinowicz, a senior researcher at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies and former head of the Iran branch in Israeli military intelligence, argued that restoring Israel's diplomatic standing requires more than a change in leadership. "If Bennett thinks he can support annexing E1 (an area east of Jerusalem where planned Israeli settlement construction could further fragment the West Bank), oppose a Palestinian state, continue the occupation of Gaza and simultaneously meet with Sisi and Abdullah and attract investment to Israel, he simply doesn't understand the depth of the international crisis," Citrinowicz said. Citrinowicz argued that without a fundamental change in Israeli policy toward the Palestinians, replacing Netanyahu would not be sufficient to restore the country's international standing. His warning comes amid changing American public attitudes toward Israel. A February 2026 Gallup survey found 36% of Americans sympathized more with Israelis, compared with 41% who sympathized more with Palestinians, a statistically insignificant five-point difference but a significant shift from the long-standing pro-Israel advantage. A comeback built on lessons from 2021 Beyond foreign policy, Bennett is promising a sweeping domestic overhaul. In an Oct. 25 manifesto, he pledged to redirect 30 billion shekels in government benefits toward families who work and serve in the military, reduce food prices by 30%, establish a state commission of inquiry into Oct. 7 and introduce an eight-year term limit for prime ministers. His alliance with Lapid gives him an established political organization, but he faces competition from Eisenkot and continuing attacks from Netanyahu, who has warned that a future opposition coalition could depend on left-wing and Arab parties. With Israel's fragmented parliamentary system requiring at least 61 seats to govern, coalition negotiations could prove as consequential as the election results themselves. Bennett has already demonstrated that political reality once. articles.title: Bombay High Court adjourns actor Imran Khan’s plea against leave India notice to Oct 27
articles.summary: Bombay High Court adjourns actor Imran Khan’s plea against FRRO “leave India” notice to Oct 27 at 3 pm; notice orders him to leave by Oct 28.
articles.body: Mumbai: Bombay high court on Monday adjourned the hearing on actor Imran Khan Pal’s petition challenging a ‘leave India’ notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), Mumbai, to Tuesday at 3 pm.Khan, represented by senior counsel V R Dhond, submitted before a bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna that the matter may be taken up on Tuesday, Oct 27, and the Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta said he had no objection to the matter being heard on Tuesday.Solicitor General Mehta, who appeared through video conferencing from Delhi, said it could be taken up at 3 pm when the CJ said an adjournment has been sought.Khan (around 44) approached the high court through lawyers Zulfiquar Memon and Parvez Memon to challenge an Oct 14 notice directing him to leave India by Oct 28. The notice was issued after an FIR was lodged against him for allegedly participating in a protest held in Mumbai on Oct 10 in support of the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi.On Monday advocate Kunal Vajani also appeared for him on VC from Delhi.In his petition, Khan challenged the Centre’s action as “arbitrary,” and in violation of his constitutional rights to equality, life and liberty under articles 14 and 21 which are available to foreigners too. He argued that it was issued without giving him a hearing and violated the principles of natural justice.Khan said he had been living in India since he was two years old and has no criminal antecedents.He e-filed his petition on Saturday.
